config.title: Design DataTable API

intro.title: Design DataTable API
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a reusable DataTable component in Vue, which displays structured data like user lists or product catalogs in a clean, tabular format. You'll learn how to design a component API by using props to make the table dynamic and configurable, allowing it to accept different datasets and column definitions. The core concept involves passing data and configuration from a parent component to the DataTable via props, enabling separation of concerns and reusability. You'll work with Vue's single-file components, JavaScript arrays and objects for data, and basic HTML table elements to structure the UI. By the end, you'll have a functional DataTable that can render any dataset you provide through its props.
intro.usecase: DataTable APIs are fundamental to enterprise dashboards and admin panels where users need to manage and analyze large datasets. In e-commerce platforms, product inventory tables use DataTable APIs to enable sorting by price, filtering by category, and pagination through thousands of items. Customer relationship management (CRM) systems rely on these APIs to display contact lists with searchable columns, bulk actions, and real-time updates. Developers implement DataTable APIs whenever they need to present structured data with interactive controls for efficient data exploration and management.

objectives: Construct a Vue component that accepts data and column definitions as props
Initialize reactive state to manage table sorting and filtering
Implement computed properties to transform and filter table data
Bind event handlers to column headers for sorting functionality
Render dynamic table rows and columns using v-for directives
Configure pagination controls to navigate through large datasets
Integrate a search input to filter table content in real-time

steps.title: Implement basic table rendering
steps.instruction: Inside the DataTable component, implement the table HTML structure with <thead> and <tbody> elements. In the <thead>, map through the columns prop to create <th> elements with each column's header text. In the <tbody>, map through the data prop to create table rows (<tr>), and within each row, map through columns again to create <td> cells displaying the corresponding data value for each column.
steps.hint: Use v-for directives to loop through columns and data. For the table body, you'll need nested loops: one for rows (data items) and another for cells (columns). Access the data value using the column's field property.
steps.analogousExample: // Example: rendering a simple table
steps.expectedOutcome: The DataTable component will render a basic HTML table structure with headers from the columns configuration and rows from the data source.
successCriteria: The component template contains a <table> with <thead> and <tbody> sections. The <thead> uses v-for to iterate over columns and render <th> elements with column headers. The <tbody> uses nested v-for loops to iterate over data items and columns to render <td> cells with the corresponding data values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you've included both the table header and body sections with proper v-for loops. Make sure you're accessing the data values using the column's field property.
steps.feedbackWrong: The table structure isn't complete. Remember to create both <thead> and <tbody> sections, use v-for to iterate through columns for headers, and use nested v-for loops for data rows and cells.
